duplicate_check.notes: No Goldfinch or Goldfinch Prime canonical platform was found in the current repository review. A full candidate audit remains required before any promotion.

notes: The first-party governance proposal moves the legacy Goldfinch protocol into recovery-only maintenance mode and winds down Goldfinch Prime. A 7 July update states that Prime investors were fully redeemed, no new deposits are accepted, and the contract was paused, while legacy V1 borrower pools remain in payment or recovery. CYA focuses on CeFi and does not prioritize DeFi lending protocols in its initial scope, so this is staged for an explicit scope and entity-boundary decision rather than forced into canonical data. Review whether Goldfinch Prime should be modeled as a historically significant institutional-yield product/platform exception, whether legacy V1 and Prime remain one platform entity, and how customer outcomes should be scoped by product.

major_event: Zipmex suspended withdrawals in July 2022 after deploying ZipUp customer assets to third-party platforms including Babel Finance and Celsius, entered Singapore restructuring proceedings, and later faced Thai enforcement and license-revocation action concerning ZipUp+ and client assets

duplicate_check.notes: Repository searches found no Zipmex, ZipUp, ZipUp+, Z Wallet, ZipLock, or Zipmex Asia canonical record or consumed candidate. The hardened candidate scanner must independently confirm this before promotion.

notes: Promote only as a product-scoped historical exchange-Earn and restructuring record. Thai SEC materials distinguish exchange custody from assets deposited through ZipUp and identify deployments to Babel Finance and Celsius. Singapore court materials cover five Zipmex entities and restructuring moratoria, not one undifferentiated legal entity. The 2024 Thai complaint concerns alleged false statements and concealed facts relating to ZipUp+ transfers; it must be recorded as a regulatory allegation and complaint, not a final fraud conviction. Current or recently updated zipmex.com pages may be repurposed or operated under a different business context and must not be treated as proof that the 2022 ZipUp obligations, creditor claims, or customer outcomes were resolved. Canonical review must separate Z Wallet, trade wallets, ZipUp/ZipUp+, regional entities, third-party counterparty exposure, restructuring proposals, individual agreements, license actions, and customer recovery by jurisdiction.

major_event: CoinFLEX suspended withdrawals in June 2022 after a manual-margin counterparty deficit later stated as US$84 million, obtained approval of a Seychelles scheme of arrangement in March 2023, and converted creditor claims into pro-rata asset distributions, recovery rights, and majority creditor equity while later litigation remained active

duplicate_check.notes: Repository searches found no CoinFLEX, Liquidity Technologies, flexUSD, rvUSD, or CoinFLEX Creditor Portal canonical record or consumed candidate. The hardened candidate scanner must independently confirm this before promotion.

notes: CoinFLEX qualifies because centralized exchange, lending, yield-bearing flexUSD, manual-margin credit, and creditor-equity conversion were economically connected but require separate product and claim boundaries. The 2026 Hong Kong High Court judgment records the June 2022 withdrawal suspension, the operator's US$84 million deficit statement, the Seychelles scheme approved on 6 March 2023, pro-rata distribution of customer assets subject to a US$10 million holdback, creditor ownership of 65% of the new holding company, and recovery rights tied to claims against the defaulting counterparty. Later disputes concerning the arbitration settlement, FLEX tokens, Fireblocks access, OPNX, and former management must not be collapsed into completed customer recovery or treated as settled facts beyond the relevant court findings. Canonical review must distinguish exchange depositors, lenders, SmartBCH holders, preferred shareholders, trade creditors, asset distributions, equity rights, recovery-value instruments, the holdback, and ongoing creditor-portal eligibility.
